claim_policy: Every deck claim must cite a repo source path, live economics Sheet, or explicit assumption. Null beats confidently wrong; no route/city IDs invented in deck copy.

sections.positioning: Build from existing Atlas Caribbean geometry; do not invent partner city coverage or route economics until each corridor has anchors.

partner_context.their_ambition: A Caribbean mobility aggregator can become the premium travel layer across fragmented island transport: airport arrivals, resort transfers, cruise/marina movements, inter-island day trips, and on-island last mile.
partner_context.their_pressure: The region is high-value but operationally fragmented: separate taxi systems, ferry timetables, resort shuttles, cruise peaks, and island-by-island regulation.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier becomes the water leg inside a door-to-door Caribbean trip stack. The partner sells the journey; Navier operates the efficient foiling marine layer.

hero.title: Caribbean Mobility Partner × Navier — one app for island-to-island premium movement
hero.subtitle: Build from existing Atlas Caribbean geometry; do not invent partner city coverage or route economics until each corridor has anchors.
hero.what_we_do_together: We package a regional premium-water mobility layer for the Caribbean: Bahamas, Puerto Rico/Spanish Virgins, USVI/BVI, Barbados, Jamaica, Dominican Republic, St Lucia/Grenadines, Turks & Caicos, Cayman, Antigua, and ABC islands. The proposal is intentionally partner-generic until an operator is chosen; the geography is Atlas-grounded, the operating model is partner-ready, and the gaps are explicit.

sections.why_now: Caribbean travel has recovered into a high-value tourism and investment cycle, while climate resilience and sustainable transport are now central policy themes. Uber's Barbados launch shows app-based mobility entering Eastern Caribbean tourist markets, but water remains the unbundled premium layer.
sections.multimodal_fit: The partner coordinates pickup, luggage/concierge, marina handoff, water transfer, and arrival ride. Navier contributes the vessel, route operating model, and clean premium experience.
proof_points: Existing Atlas Caribbean nodes found in data-clean: Nassau/Bahamas, Puerto Rico, USVI/BVI, Barbados, Jamaica, Samaná/Dominican Republic, St Lucia/Grenadines, Turks & Caicos, Cayman, Antigua, ABC islands.
Uber Barbados 2025 launch: Uber Taxi officially available across Barbados and first Eastern Caribbean launch.
Tourism Analytics: Caribbean tourism data platform covering 33+ destinations / 40+ destinations language on site.
OECD Caribbean Development Dynamics 2026: region requires faster and higher-quality investment amid climate risks and structural vulnerabilities.

objections.objection: There is no named Caribbean platform partner yet.
objections.response: Correct. This is a generic mobility-partner blueprint with exact market readiness; once a partner is named, only the partner footprint/evidence layer changes.

objections.objection: Country refs are missing for many Caribbean markets.
objections.response: Do not run final economics until country-reference rows and demand anchors are added. The gap queue names that explicitly.

objections.objection: Inter-island routes can exceed N30 range or trigger customs/regulatory complexity.
objections.response: Use short commercial-now routes first; mark long/cross-border routes as Quanta-LR or authority-dependent roadmap.

objections.objection: Tourism volume does not equal water demand.
objections.response: Correct; tourism sources prioritize markets, but corridor economics need route-specific ferry/visitor/airport/resort demand anchors before gold economics.
